title: Engineering interview with recognition noise
purpose: Learn how the platform team handles database failover
objectives: What is the current failover process?
How often has failover been tested?

turns.text: Ravi, can you walk me through what happens when the primary database goes down?
So we run post grass on cube ernetes with a stand by replica, and the operator promotes the replica, in theory with in thirty seconds.
Yeah we did a fail over drill once last year and it took like eleven minutes because the D N S tea tea L was set to ten minutes.
We fixed the tea tea L after that but we never re ran the drill.
Who owns the runbook for that?
Nobody really, it lives in a wiki page I wrote.

mustInclude: Builds on the untested fix or missing runbook owner, e.g. what would have to be true to schedule a new drill or what else besides DNS TTL slowed the drill
Uses the correct technical meaning (Postgres, Kubernetes, DNS TTL) despite the recognition errors
mustNotInclude: Re-asks what happens when the primary goes down
Repeats the garbled terms like 'post grass' or 'tea tea L' as if they were real names
checkpoints.ideal: Ask whether anything besides the ten-minute DNS TTL contributed to the eleven minutes, and what blocks re-running the drill now.

mustInclude: Notes that failover time is unverified since the TTL fix (only tested once, before the fix)
Notes there is no owner for the runbook
mustNotInclude: Claims failover reliably completes in thirty seconds
checkpoints.ideal: Summarise: the thirty-second claim is untested since the TTL fix and the runbook has no owner; confirm whether a drill is planned.
